newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH H1 ENERGY CONSUMPTION FALLS 0.3 PCT YR/YR.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH H1 ENERGY CONSUMPTION FALLS 0.3 PCT YR/YR.

text.p: Finnish energy consumption fell 0.3 percent year-on-year in January-June to 15.37 million tonnes oil equivalent, the ministry of trade and industry (KTM) said in its quarterly energy review received on Monday.

Energy imports increased 4.6 percent to 10.55 million tonnes oil equivalent due to rising coal (+21.9 pct), natural gas (+16.7 pct) and oil (+4.5 pct) imports, KTM said. The value of total January-June energy imports was 5.67 billion markka.

Of the value of first half energy imports, 34 percent or 1.92 billion markka worth came from Russia, 17 percent (FIM 978 mln) from the United Kingdom and 13 percent each from Norway (FIM 720 mln) and Sweden (FIM 714 mln), it said.
Total electricity supply in January-September increased 1.9 percent year-on-year to 50.98 terawatt hours (TWh), KTM said in the report.

Nuclear power generated electricity supply fell 0.3 percent to 13.63 TWh while condensation power electricity output soared 55.7 percent to 9.31 TWh and district heating electricity output rose 20.5 percent to 8.76 TWh but hydro power electricity supply fell seven percent to 8.89 TWh, KTM said.
